metadata.title: Nepal pavement screening model
metadata.price_basis: Illustrative constant NPR at analysis date; not market-verified estimates
metadata.functional_unit: 1 km of 7 m carriageway; common 1.5 m total shoulder width outside carriageway
metadata.scope: Reconstruction on an existing, stable, accessible alignment; no land, major earthworks, major structures or utility relocation
metadata.structural_status: Illustrative section quantities only. No traffic, CBR, fatigue, drainage or flexural design performed.
metadata.lcc_boundary: Agency direct construction + design/supervision + maintenance - residual credit. Excludes VAT, contingency, user delay, vehicle operating cost and emissions. Not a full economic appraisal.
metadata.residual_policy: Common assets, pavement structure and localized slab repairs assumed consumed by year30. Remaining asphalt surfacing service credited pro rata from last renewal, including preparatory work as part of renewal service. No recycling cash credit for either pavement.
metadata.schedule_warning: All intervention intervals are scenarios, not Nepal field service-life measurements. Concrete does not eliminate drainage, foundation or landslide failures.

common_items.name: Formation preparation and compaction
common_items.note: Existing stable alignment; excludes new embankment and deep weak-ground treatment.

common_items.name: Granular subbase, 200 mm compacted
common_items.note: Illustrative quantity; same common layer in both concepts, not a design recommendation.

common_items.name: Side drains, both sides
common_items.note: Concept allowance for lined side drains; dimensions require catchment and outfall design.

common_items.name: Cross-drain/outfall rehabilitation allowance
common_items.note: No new major culverts, bridges or flood-protection structures included.

common_items.name: Shoulders, 0.75 m each side
common_items.note: Shoulders are outside the equal 7 m carriageway.

common_items.name: Signs, markings, traffic management and contractor QA

flexible_items.name: Wet-mix macadam, 200 mm compacted
flexible_items.note: Illustrative base, to be redesigned after axle counts and soaked CBR.

flexible_items.name: Dense bituminous macadam, 60 mm
flexible_items.note: Installed mix assumption includes materials, local haul, plant, labour and contractor margin.

flexible_items.name: Asphalt concrete surface, 40 mm
flexible_items.note: Not a quoted Nepal contract rate; long haul and remote sites can exceed range.

flexible_items.name: Prime and tack coats
flexible_items.note: Combined coat allowance, not a binder application-rate specification.

concrete_items.name: Dry lean concrete subbase, 150 mm
concrete_items.note: Illustrative support layer; DoR requires at least 7 days before placing slab.

concrete_items.name: Jointed plain concrete slab, 250 mm
concrete_items.note: Includes placing and curing; flexural design and approved mix must determine thickness.

concrete_items.name: Dowels, ties, joints, sawing and sealing
concrete_items.note: Separate from slab rate to avoid omitting joints or counting them twice.

concrete_items.name: Separation membrane
concrete_items.note: Concept allowance; detailed interface specification by pavement designer.

selection_matrix.scale: 1=poor; 5=strong. Except cost ratios, scores and all weights are subjective screening judgments.

criteria.name: 30-year agency cost
criteria.reason: Calculated: score=5 × lowest modeled LCC / option LCC. Model uncertainty remains.

criteria.name: Initial budget affordability
criteria.reason: Calculated: score=5 × lowest base capex / option capex. Separate liquidity constraint; overlaps cost deliberately.

criteria.name: Fit to a varied corridor
criteria.reason: Judgment: C targets permanent high-stress locations; A less suited to assumed slow/heavy load stress; B sacrifices flexibility on ordinary stretches. Depends on successful diagnosis, drainage and stable foundations.

criteria.name: Deliverability and quality control
criteria.reason: Judgment: established asphalt supply versus additional concrete paving, joint and curing skills; C needs both and transition management.

criteria.name: Recurring maintenance burden
criteria.reason: Judgment: asphalt needs more frequent interventions under assumed service lives; concrete still needs joints, slabs and drain upkeep. Overlaps LCC only for non-cash management reliability.

criteria.name: Domestic supply and import exposure
criteria.reason: Judgment: concrete uses domestic cement, with fuel/equipment/inputs still partly imported; asphalt also uses local aggregate and labour. Not a quantified foreign-exchange saving.

criteria.name: Construction access and reopening
criteria.reason: Judgment: concrete new-construction 28-day traffic closure per DoR; staged partial-width work may maintain access but does not waive cure requirement.

criteria.name: Utility access and staged adaptation
criteria.reason: Judgment: asphalt easier to cut, restore and strengthen; concrete most suitable after utility conflicts resolved.

criteria.name: Environmental evidence
criteria.reason: Neutral placeholder: no Nepal mix EPDs, haul inventory, recycling or vehicle-use model. No environmental winner claimed.

selection_matrix.warning: Scores are not measured field performance. Weight sweeps and scenario counts are not probabilities. No carbon preference until inventory exists.

construction_productivity.status: Illustrative resource planning, not a contractor programme. Productive days exclude monsoon, breakdowns, approvals, preparation, haul constraints and curing.
construction_productivity.closure_note: For new DoR concrete pavement, require minimum28-day traffic closure after slab placement and at least7 days from DLC to slab; detailed engineer-reviewed programme governs.

sensitivity.interpretation: Deterministic grid, not a probability distribution; many scenarios deliberately include zero stressed share, where A and C coincide.
